title: Mukhtasar al-Quduri
author: al-quduri
attributionNote: The attribution is the one the manuscript tradition and the scholarship give.
description: The most widely studied primer of Hanafi law: a terse statement of the school's rulings from purification and prayer to inheritance, written to be memorised. Later authors built whole libraries of commentary on it, and al-Marghinani's al-Hidaya, already on this shelf, draws on it directly.
historicalContext: Al-Quduri led the Hanafis of Baghdad in the early eleventh century. His Mukhtasar became one of the 'three texts' of the school's curriculum and was taught from Anatolia to India for nine centuries.
availabilityNote: Arabic text only, streamed from OpenITI at read time. No English translation is included because no public-domain English translation was verified. Only the catalogue record, chapter outline and passage index are held here.
